title: Regional fan-in failover and soft-degrade protocols for request-level load funneling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a region-aware "fan-in" failover and soft-degradation protocol that shapes incoming traffic at the admission layer to preserve SLOs during cross-region outages and transient capacity shortages. The goal is to avoid hard global outages by (1) funneling requests to regional fallback paths while preserving high-priority traffic, (2) offering progressive fidelity reductions at the response level, and (3) limiting blast radius via origin-based credits and grace windows.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller can apply per-origin credits and enforce fan-in limits per region
Requests can be downgraded by fidelity tier (streaming -> summary -> microresponse) with deterministic partial responses returned when applicable
System maintains >95% of P90 latency SLO for P0 customers during simulated region failover with up to 40% reduced capacity in primary region
Operator tools show real-time fan-in ratios, tenant spillover tokens, and per-tier success rates in Console
Automated canary rollout of the policy with ability to rollback in <5 minutes
design_notes: Context: previous incidents showed cascading retries from east-west failover caused overload in healthy regions. This design focuses on shaping at the source: per-origin tokens, directional spillover, and deterministic degradation modes.
detailed_spec:
Key components:
- Origin Credits: a per-tenant, per-region credit bucket that decays on spillover and replenishes on stable windows. Defaults derived from historical traffic and SLA tier.
- Fan-in Gate: a region-local admission gate that enforces a configurable max inbound ratio from remote origins (fan-in limit). Must operate in <2ms on hot path.
- Directional Spillover: when fan-in hits threshold, low-priority traffic is nudged to stored fallback variants or delayed-short queues; high-priority traffic bypasses with token charge.
- Soft-degrade Modes: fidelity ladder defined as [full-response, partial-prefix, summary, microresponse]. Degradation applied at response generation stage with deterministic trimming to preserve semantics (avoid hallucination).
- Grace Windows: when a failover starts, allow short burst (configurable seconds) where fan-in is lenient to absorb transient spikes; after window, strict limits apply.
- Observability: metrics (fan_in_ratio, origin_credit_balance, degraded_response_rate), traces linking admission decision to final response quality metric.
- Backpressure Integration: admit decisions publish to central coordinator for cross-region view, enabling adaptive fan-in tuning based on remote queue lengths.
tradeoffs:
- Complexity: origin credits and directional logic add bookkeeping; mitigated by sharded in-memory stores and bounded retention.
- Determinism vs Flexibility: We choose a deterministic fidelity ladder for predictable downstream behavior at the cost of slightly higher implementation surface.
- Latency impact: fan-in gate must be extremely cheap; implemented as a single lookup and atomic debit in region-local cache to avoid RPCs.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated; deploy to EU region as canary with default conservative limits. 2) Run 48h shadow mode (decisions logged but not enforced) and compare to baseline. 3) Enable enforcement for 5% of traffic, monitor Console dashboards. 4) Gradually ramp to 100% while adjusting defaults. 5) Post-mortem and tuning cycle.
monitoring: Dashboards: Region Fan-in Overview, Origin Credit Heatmap, Degradation Ladder Impact. Alerts: >10% degraded_rate for P0 customers over 5m, origin_credit_balance < 5% for >10 tenants, sudden jump in cross-region spillover. Grafana and PagerDuty integration documented in runbook.
tasks: Implement origin credit store and API (sharded in-memory + write-behind to durable store)
Add fan-in gate to admission hot path with unit and perf tests
Integrate degradation ladder into runtime response generator and ensure deterministic trimming rules
Add metrics and tracing hooks to link admission decisions to final model outputs
Create Console widgets and alert rules for operator visibility
Run chaos tests simulating 30-50% capacity loss in region and validate SLO preservation
Write runbook for incident response and operator controls (override fan-in, drain tokens)
comments: 2025-11-06 Marco Gutierrez: Spike complete for credit store options. Favor in-memory LRU shards with periodic reconciliation to postgres. Perf sketch shows <1ms median debit. Moving to prototyping.

2026-01-12 Lina Zhou (SRE): Added initial dashboard mocks and suggested alert thresholds. Concern: default grace window of 120s may be too long for rapid failover — recommend 30s. Updated spec accordingly.
2026-02-02 Product review: PM requested explicit customer controls to opt-out of cross-region spillover for regulated tenants. Added tenant flag and unit tests planned.
2026-02-18 Engineering review: Code PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128) for admission gate; integration tests failing on race in debit path. Investigating atomicity edge cases.

2026-03-05 QA: Ran chaos experiment in staging simulating eu-west outage. Shadow mode logs show expected 3x reduction in low-priority acceptance; high-priority retention at 98%. Need to tune replenishment backoff to avoid long tail.
2026-03-10 Marco Gutierrez: Fixed race by moving debit to compare-and-swap on shard; perf regression 0.3ms median — acceptable. Preparing canary deployment to eu region behind feature flag.
